stages.title: Chapters 1-4
stages.note: The main story spine. These awards arrive on their own; the real work is not rushing past the strands that open alongside them.

stages.title: The finale
stages.note: The last mission and the end of the story. Everything missable in the later stages has to be closed before you start it.

stages.title: Front-loaded story missions
stages.note: Single-mission awards that appear while the plot runs. Automatic, but listed in playing order so the roadmap reads straight through.

stages.title: 100% completion
stages.note: The long gold. Trust the in-game checklist over any external list, including this one.

stages.title: Activities and skill gates
stages.note: Stunts, ranges, races, meditation and arcade games. Repeatable and never missable, so save them for whenever you need a change of pace.

stages.title: Stranger strands
stages.note: Companion and stranger chains. Every missable trophy in the guide sits here; finish each strand inside the chapter that opens it.

stages.title: Collectibles and coverage
stages.note: Cards, WAiNK spots, vehicle discovery and map fog. Route these district by district in a single sweep.

stages.title: Heists and robberies
stages.note: Banks, trucks, shops and gang operations. The escape is part of the requirement every single time.

stages.title: Economy and decisions
stages.note: Money loops, property and the hidden choice trophies. Left last because they need cash and a save file you can return to.

stages.title: The platinum
stages.note: The receipt. It appears once the other fifty-four are already on the shelf.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: Nothing new is asked of you here: the platinum simply confirms that the other fifty-four are already earned. Treat it as a receipt rather than a target, and spend your planning on the two golds that set the length of the run. The only real failure mode is a closed missable window, so audit the roadmap before the final chapter.
trophies.why: It asks nothing of its own and everything of the list beneath it.
steps: Earn the other fifty-four trophies.
The platinum unlocks with whichever trophy finishes the set.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing sits near the front of the story chain, so follow the markers until it appears and play it through. There is no optional objective to worry about, but let the closing scene run instead of skipping it, because the award is written at the end of the mission. Finishing the last objective is all the trophy wants.
trophies.why: An early story mission with no branch and no failure state.
steps: Play the story mission Gone Fishing.
Let the results screen appear.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 ends after its epilogue mission, which plenty of players mistake for side content and leave sitting on the map. Clear every marker the chapter offers, including the short follow-up after the main arc, then let the transition play out. The trophy lands on the chapter boundary, and that same boundary is where Leonida's missable clock starts.
trophies.why: Cheap to earn, but the chapter line quietly closes the first missable windows.
steps: Complete every Chapter 1 mission, epilogue included.
The trophy pops when the chapter closes.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 widens the map and introduces most of the strands that can later expire. Push the mission chain while opening every new strand marker you pass, so nothing is left half-finished when the chapter flips. The trophy only needs the mission set, but the housekeeping you do here decides whether the platinum stays possible.
trophies.why: Story progress on paper, a deadline in practice.
steps: Complete every Chapter 2 mission.
Open any stranger strand the chapter reveals before moving on.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: By Chapter 3 the state is crowded with money-making distractions and it is easy to let the plot stall for hours. Keep the chapter chain moving and treat any story-adjacent job as mandatory until it is done. Check the strand list before the closing mission, because this boundary can retire one you opened and forgot about.
trophies.why: Automatic if you keep moving, punishing if you wander.
steps: Complete every Chapter 3 mission.
Audit open strands before the chapter closes.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last runway before the ending, so use it as an audit rather than a sprint. Work through the missions, then walk the roadmap for open strands, one-time social beats and decision trophies you meant to save. Cross into the finale only when the list is clean; the trophy itself merely asks for the chapter's missions.
trophies.why: The chapter is easy; arriving here with unfinished business is what costs the platinum.
steps: Complete every Chapter 4 mission.
Clear the roadmap before starting the finale.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: This gold rewards finishing the story rather than surviving a hard fight, so prepare the save file before you launch the mission. Close every missable strand, bank the decision trophies and keep a manual save in case you want the other branch. Then play from the mission start to the credits without quitting, because the completion flag is set at the end of the epilogue.
trophies.why: A gold for the ending rather than for the difficulty.
steps: Finish everything the story requires before the finale.
Complete the final mission and watch through the epilogue.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a single story job on the early mission chain, so the work is reaching it and finishing every objective. Stay with the scripted chase instead of trying to shortcut it, since the trigger usually waits for a scene to finish. The trophy pops on the results screen.
trophies.why: One mission, one objective, no branches.
steps: Reach and play Breakfast Run.
Complete the final objective.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist, so the setup jobs and the finale all have to be completed in sequence. Take the optional prep the game offers, because skipping it makes the escape harder without saving meaningful time. The trophy is tied to the heist's completion screen rather than to the size of the take.
trophies.why: A plot heist with a fixed crew and a fixed outcome.
steps: Complete the heist's setup missions.
Finish The Cartel Heist finale.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a mid-story mission with a scripted outcome, so play it at a normal pace and let the scenes finish. There is nothing to collect or protect beyond what the mission tells you, and a failed checkpoint simply restarts you nearby. Clear the last objective for the trophy.
trophies.why: Story furniture: unmissable, quick and impossible to spoil.
steps: Play the story mission Child's Play.
Complete the mission.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners sits on the main chain and is easy to rush past while chasing map icons. Complete the objectives in the order given and let the wrap-up scene finish before you open the phone or travel away. The trophy arrives with the mission-complete screen.
trophies.why: A single mid-game mission with no optional conditions.
steps: Play Headliners.
Finish the mission without leaving early.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is a set-piece mission, so expect a scripted approach and a scripted escape. Follow the prompts rather than improvising, watch for an objective timer if one appears, and let the mission end cleanly. The award is unconditional once the mission completes.
trophies.why: A fixed set-piece with nothing missable inside it.
steps: Play VCIA Takedown.
Follow the scripted escape to the end.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is one of the louder story missions and it closes a chapter's worth of setup. Bring armour and a reliable rifle, use cover during the assault, and do not leave the mission area early. The trophy unlocks with the mission, and the mission ends when the script says so.
trophies.why: Harder than it looks in the moment, but structurally unmissable.
steps: Start Operation Savage Glory with armour and rifle ammo.
Complete the assault and the extraction.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: 100% is the long pole, and the in-game checklist is the authority rather than any external list. Work region by region: story and strangers first, then collectibles and activities, then vehicles and properties, because the later categories get easier once traversal is fully unlocked. Keep a manual save before the final mission so you can mop up whatever the checklist still flags.
trophies.why: The endurance test: it is all of a very large state, not just all of the story.
steps: Clear story and stranger content.
Sweep collectibles, activities, vehicles and properties.
Reconcile against the in-game checklist until it reads 100%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Two hundred and fifty stunts is a grind best done in circuits rather than one at a time. Pick a district with dense ramps, repeat a jump you can land reliably, and rotate areas when the run starts to feel stale. The counter only cares about distinct stunts, so keep track of which ones you have already banked.
trophies.why: No skill ceiling, just a long and repetitive count.
steps: Find a district with several reliable stunt jumps.
Land each unique stunt cleanly so it registers.
Rotate districts until the counter passes 250.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: This one rewards sampling rather than mastering, so open the activity list and work down it once. Golf, tennis, darts, racing, hunting and the arcade all count, and each just needs a completed session rather than a win. Keep a short checklist so you do not repeat a category and leave another untouched.
trophies.why: Breadth over depth: one pass through every activity type is enough.
steps: Open the activity menu and list the categories.
Complete one session of each.
Check the trophy after the last new category.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold at the range comes down to route memory and ammo discipline. Learn each challenge's target order on a silver run, then replay for time and accuracy, reloading between strings instead of during them. Do the whole range in one sitting so the feel of the weapon stays with you.
trophies.why: A pure execution test with a fixed, learnable target pattern.
steps: Earn a silver on each challenge to learn the target order.
Replay for time and accuracy without wasting rounds.
Bank gold on every challenge.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Each Top Fun location has its own course and only a win counts, so learn the route before racing for real. Cut inside on corners, save the boost for straights, and treat a second place as a free practice lap. Clear the locations district by district to avoid crossing the state twice.
trophies.why: Several short races where course knowledge beats raw piloting.
steps: Find every Top Fun drone race location.
Learn each course, then win it.
Repeat until every location shows a win.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Any race type counts as long as it is a different event, so spread wins across street, off-road and water races instead of farming one favourite. Winning against the easiest available field is perfectly fine. Note which events you have already won so the twentieth is not a repeat.
trophies.why: A variety requirement wearing a skill requirement's clothes.
steps: List the race events on the map.
Win twenty distinct events, any class.
Check the counter before repeating a favourite.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal's fishing challenge opens during his strand and can be lost for good if you finish the strand or the chapter without taking it. Fish the deeper water he points you toward, use the lure that suits it, and be patient on the reel instead of snapping the line. Beat his total in a single session to close the strand cleanly.
trophies.why: A friendly contest with a hard deadline attached to someone else's story.
steps: Progress Cal's strand until the challenge is offered.
Accept it immediately and fish the spots he marks.
Beat his total before leaving the area.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Any arcade cabinet in Leonida counts, so pick the shortest game rather than the most fun. Learn the first two stages, then spend continues freely, because the trophy only checks that the credits roll. Playing a cabinet indoors also avoids interruptions from the street.
trophies.why: One completed arcade run, with no requirement to be good at it.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet.
Play one game through to its ending, using continues.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's strand runs for several missions and the trophy only fires on his last one, so do not stop halfway. His calls arrive on a timer, which means ignoring the phone for a few chapters can quietly end the strand. Finish every request he gives, then complete the final mission before advancing the plot.
trophies.why: The last step of a multi-mission strand that can lapse between chapters.
steps: Answer Andy's calls and finish each job.
Complete his final mission before the chapter turns over.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's jobs are water-focused and only the last one awards the trophy, so treat every call from him as urgent. Missing a call or letting a chapter boundary pass can close the strand permanently. Complete his chain in one stretch, ideally with a fast boat already docked nearby.
trophies.why: A strand finale that punishes players who save his jobs for later.
steps: Take Kenton's calls as they arrive.
Complete every boat job in his chain.
Finish his final mission before the chapter ends.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand is a short chain with a definitive last job, and the trophy is tied to that job alone. Take his calls as they come and finish each mission before starting something long, because the strand does not wait through a chapter change. Only the final mission matters for the award.
trophies.why: Short chain, sharp deadline.
steps: Progress Billy's strand as soon as it opens.
Complete the chain's final mission.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight complete strands is a breadth requirement, not a depth one, so count strands rather than missions. Each one has to be finished to its final job; a half-done strand contributes nothing. Use the map's stranger markers and clear the shortest chains first so the count climbs predictably.
trophies.why: Eight finished stories rather than eight started ones.
steps: Track each stranger strand to its final mission.
Finish eight strands in total.
Confirm the counter before assuming a strand counted.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand revolves around supply runs, and the trophy lands on his last job. His missions arrive in bursts, so clear each one before the next story beat pushes the strand aside. If a chapter boundary is close, finish Randy first; the window does not reopen.
trophies.why: Another strand finale that closes with the chapter.
steps: Complete each of Randy's supply jobs in order.
Finish his final mission before advancing the story.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's chain is easy to start and easy to forget, and only the final mission pays the trophy. Work through his jobs in order, keep the vehicle he asks for in good condition, and do not launch a long story mission while one of his calls is pending. Finish the strand before the map moves on.
trophies.why: A late strand step that most players lose by procrastinating.
steps: Answer Tyrone and complete his early jobs.
Keep the requested vehicle intact.
Complete his final mission before the chapter ends.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: The meditation spots are scattered across the whole state and each needs a full session rather than a quick visit. Sit through the sequence until the prompt clears, then move on, because leaving early does not count. Sweep them by region alongside other collectible work so the travel is shared.
trophies.why: A calm, low-skill checklist that is only tedious if left to the end.
steps: Locate every meditation spot on the map.
Complete a full session at each one.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret's hunting request is a one-time side job, and it disappears if his strand is left too long. Travel to the marker he gives you, track the animal instead of shooting at movement in the brush, and take a clean shot so the carcass registers. Deliver it to close the request and the trophy.
trophies.why: A single animal, a single window, and no second invitation.
steps: Accept Bret's hunting request when it appears.
Track and kill the unique animal cleanly.
Deliver the carcass to Bret.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Card sets are regional, so finish one district's set before starting another or you will lose track of which cards are missing. The in-game collectible menu shows progress per set; use it instead of a mental list. Three complete sets is the requirement, not three nearly complete ones.
trophies.why: Collection discipline across three separate sets.
steps: Pick a district and collect its full card set.
Repeat for two more sets, checking the menu after each pickup.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK check-ins are Leonida's version of a photo album, and a hundred of them is a travel project. Interact at each marker until the confirmation appears, then move on, because partial interactions do not bank. Group them by neighbourhood so you are not crossing the state for single locations.
trophies.why: A pure numbers trophy that rewards a planned route.
steps: Enable WAiNK locations on the map.
Check in at each until the counter confirms.
Work neighbourhood by neighbourhood to 100.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges are the small optional objectives the game tracks in the background, and fifty accumulate naturally if you keep an eye on the list. Pick the ones close to whatever you are already doing rather than chasing distant ones. Each completed challenge banks individually, so progress is never lost.
trophies.why: Fifty small tasks that reward opportunism over planning.
steps: Open the challenge list and note nearby entries.
Complete fifty challenges across the state.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: This needs a four-star chase survived with your partner in the car, so start it deliberately rather than by accident. Drive out of the city on the highway, break line of sight, then wait in a side street until the stars fade. Do not switch vehicles mid-chase; the escape only counts once the level is fully clear.
trophies.why: A deliberate, high-heat escape that is easy to overshoot or abandon.
steps: Build a four-star wanted level with your partner aboard.
Break line of sight and stay in the car until the stars clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Plan three shops within a short drive of each other and hit them in one continuous run. The wanted level has to stay live between robberies, so do not stop to shake the police; keep moving and use the getaway car. The trophy fires after the third escape, not after the third till.
trophies.why: Route planning under pressure, with no room to cool off.
steps: Scout three shops close together.
Rob all three without letting the wanted level expire.
Escape after the third.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discovery means getting close enough for the game to log the model, not owning it. Park near busy districts and let traffic cycle, or walk a dealership row and note each model as it registers. The garage list is your tracker, so check it before driving across the state for one specific car.
trophies.why: A patience and observation trophy rather than a driving test.
steps: Check the garage list for models still missing.
Scan traffic-heavy areas and dealerships to log them.
Reach 100 discovered vehicles.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Combat Focus drains quickly, so the five targets need to be close together and visible before you trigger it. Set up a group encounter, activate Focus only when three or more are in frame, and chain headshots without pausing to reload. A failed attempt costs nothing but the cooldown.
trophies.why: A short burst of precision with a hard count inside one window.
steps: Find a group of five or more enemies.
Activate Combat Focus and chain five kills before it ends.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: VCIA has a runway long enough to take a vehicle where it should not go. Get airside without triggering a lockdown, line up on the runway and get airborne before the response closes the gates. Any aircraft works; the award is for the departure, not the landing.
trophies.why: A stunt with a bit of nerve and a very clear success condition.
steps: Get airside at VCIA without raising a lockdown.
Take off from the runway before the response closes in.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The Rhino is a military vehicle and the trophy is for taking one somewhere it does not belong. Find the base's vehicle spawn, get in before the alert escalates, and drive out through the least defended gate. Once you are clear the trophy is yours; you do not have to keep the tank.
trophies.why: A theft with a short window and a forgiving payoff.
steps: Enter the military base and reach a Rhino.
Drive it out through a gate before the alert locks down.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Detection is the entire requirement, so scout the store before you touch a display. Disable the alarm, deal with or avoid the staff quietly, and leave before the response is called. If a star appears, reload the save rather than fighting your way out.
trophies.why: The only failure state is noise.
steps: Scout the store and disable the alarm.
Take the jewellery without triggering detection.
Leave before any wanted level appears.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Five vaults means five separate robberies with a successful escape each, so treat them as a campaign rather than a spree. Learn one crew setup that works, apply it to every bank, and keep a fast car parked on the route out. The trophy counts escapes, so the getaway matters as much as the vault.
trophies.why: Five repetitions of the same high-risk job with no shortcuts.
steps: Plan a crew setup and getaway route that work.
Rob five bank vaults, escaping cleanly each time.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks are moving targets, so hit one where the route slows: a junction, a tunnel mouth or a depot entrance. Block the road, take the cargo, and leave before the escort responds. The escape is part of the requirement, so plan the exit before you stop the truck.
trophies.why: One job, but the getaway is graded as strictly as the robbery.
steps: Ambush an armored truck where its route slows.
Take the cargo and escape before the escort arrives.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Exploration fills in as you physically enter each region, so drive the coast and the inland highways rather than fast-travelling everywhere. Fog on the map is the tracker: if a patch is still grey, you have not been there. Combine the sweep with vehicle discovery and WAiNK check-ins.
trophies.why: A map-coverage trophy that rewards wandering instead of objectives.
steps: Drive every region until the map fog clears.
Combine the sweep with collectibles and vehicle discovery.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Each gang runs a different illegal operation, and the trophy wants one of each rather than several of one. Identify which gang owns each operation from the intel menu, then hit them in any order. Escapes count, so bring a vehicle that can take a few bumps.
trophies.why: Variety across the criminal map, one operation per gang.
steps: Identify each gang's illegal operation.
Rob one operation belonging to every gang.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: This is a one-time social beat on Ocean Beach and it only counts at the right moment in the story. When the prompt appears, take the drink and stay for the scene instead of walking away. It cannot be repeated once the chapter moves on.
trophies.why: A quiet, one-shot moment that most players skip past.
steps: Wait for the Ocean Beach prompt during the story.
Take the cocktail and stay through the scene.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: The showroom escape wants you to leave through the glass in a car, not through the door on foot. Pick the fastest car on the floor, get a run-up, and aim for the largest window. The trophy registers the moment you are outside with the vehicle still driveable.
trophies.why: A single absurd stunt with an obvious, satisfying trigger.
steps: Enter a vehicle showroom.
Take a car and drive it through the front glass.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: The bowling beat is a story-adjacent social event and it only counts once. Finish the full game rather than leaving after a frame, and stay for the conversation that follows. If the chapter ends first, the opportunity is gone.
trophies.why: One frame too few and the moment is lost.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley when invited.
Finish the game and stay for the scene.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This decision trophy is tied to how you handle the public-facing partnership late in the story. Build the relationship the mission asks for, take the visible option rather than the quiet one, and let the resulting scene play. Choices like this are why a manual save before the final chapters is worth keeping.
trophies.why: A hidden choice trophy with no second chances after the ending.
steps: Progress the late-story partnership missions.
Choose the public option and let the scene resolve.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: This one tracks a decision rather than a skill, and it is awarded when that choice resolves in a later scene. Commit to one path instead of hedging, and do not reload to explore both options until the trophy has popped. A manual save beforehand lets you see the other branch safely.
trophies.why: The game is grading your intent, not your execution.
steps: Keep a manual save before the decision point.
Commit to a choice and play the resolution scene.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description hints at a retry, and that is exactly what it wants: attempt the relevant beat, fail or decline the first time, then come back for the second. Do not reload past the first attempt, because the second only counts if the first happened in the same save. The trophy lands when the second attempt resolves.
trophies.why: A hidden trophy that requires you to fail once on purpose.
steps: Attempt the beat and let the first try fail.
Return and complete it on the second attempt.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: This is the strangest of the late-story awards and it comes from following the odd thread rather than the obvious one. When an unusual opportunity appears near the end, take it and see it through instead of dismissing it. The trophy fires on the resolution scene.
trophies.why: A curiosity reward for players who chase the weird option.
steps: Watch for the unusual late-story opportunity.
Follow it through to its resolution scene.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: This is a stunt rather than a bowling trophy: drive alongside a pedestrian and strike them from the car in one pass. Keep the speed moderate so the hit registers as melee rather than a collision, then drive away before the response builds. Any busy street works.
trophies.why: A one-move stunt with an unhelpfully gentle description.
steps: Drive slowly alongside a pedestrian.
Strike them from the car in a single pass.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills have to be cleaned through your contacts, and the total is cumulative across the whole game. Run the laundering loop whenever you have a stack rather than hoarding until the end, and use the contact with the best rate. The trophy tracks money laundered, not money earned.
trophies.why: A cumulative economy goal that only rewards patience.
steps: Collect Marked Bills from robberies and jobs.
Launder them through contacts until $250,000 is processed.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spending counts across every shop type, so spread purchases rather than buying one expensive car. Clothing, weapons, tattoos, food and property upgrades all feed the same total. The counter is cumulative, so early spending is never wasted.
trophies.why: The easiest economy trophy if you spend as you play.
steps: Buy across clothing, weapons, food and upgrades.
Keep spending until the total passes $100,000.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Every garage property has to be bought, which makes this a money gate rather than a skill gate. Save the property list for after the story's big paydays, then buy them in price order so the cheap ones are not forgotten. Ownership, not use, is what counts.
trophies.why: The most expensive checkbox on the list.
steps: Save cash from the story's major payouts.
Buy every garage property on the map.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Scooter Bros registration is quick but easy to ignore, so do it as you steal or buy scooters. Each registration needs a distinct vehicle, so vary the model rather than re-registering the same one. Ten is a short list if you register every scooter you pass.
trophies.why: A small habit repeated ten times.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app with a scooter in hand.
Register ten distinct vehicles.
